title: Normality ascends along smooth morphisms
statement: Let $g:V\to W$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose $W$ is normal, meaning that every local ring $\mathcal O_{W,w}$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then every local ring $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ is an integrally closed domain, so $V$ is normal. No Noetherian, quasi-compactness, connectedness, or surjectivity assumption is imposed; empty schemes are allowed.

source.place: Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth, ascent part of its proof.

proof.text: Fix $v\in V$ and put $w=g(v)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] on $W$ to choose an affine open $B$ containing $w$, then on $V$ to the open $g^{-1}(B)$ to choose an affine open $A$ with $v\in A\subseteq g^{-1}(B)$. Set $R=\mathcal O_W(B)$ and $S=\mathcal O_V(A)$, and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be the section map induced by $g$. These choices concern a single point and require no finite affine cover.

source.place: Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth, affine ascent paragraph; choice of affine charts via Schemes Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens.

proof.text: Let $j_A:A\to V$ and $j_B:B\to W$ be the open inclusions. Since $g(A)\subseteq B$, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives a unique $g_{A,B}:A\to B$ with $j_B\circ g_{A,B}=g\circ j_A$, and $g_{A,B}$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a). The map $\varphi:R\to S$ of step 1 is $g^\sharp_B:\mathcal O_W(B)\to\mathcal O_V(g^{-1}(B))$ followed by restriction to $A$. Let $\iota_A:\operatorname{Spec}S\to V$, $\iota_B:\operatorname{Spec}R\to W$ be the canonical open immersions of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], so $\iota_A=j_A\circ\alpha$, $\iota_B=j_B\circ\beta$ for the isomorphisms $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}S\to A$, $\beta:\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], $\iota_B\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=g\circ\iota_A$, so $j_B\circ(\beta\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi)=j_B\circ(g_{A,B}\circ\alpha)$, and the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives $\beta\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=g_{A,B}\circ\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](c) with $u=\alpha$, $v=\beta$, $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] $\varphi$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], the notion used by the ring theorem in step 4. This is Morphisms 01V6 (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) for the chosen pair; the definition alone gives only some affine pair around each point, so this step is not elementary.

source.place: Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize, (1) implies (2), with the affine identification of More on Morphisms Tag 02H6 as recorded in lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine.

proof.text: For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the affine chart $B\simeq\operatorname{Spec}R$ gives a point $b\in B$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $R_{\mathfrak p}\simeq\mathcal O_{W,b}$. The latter is an integrally closed domain by the hypothesis on $W$, so the former is as well: a ring isomorphism preserves nonzero products and carries monic integral equations and their solutions in fraction fields to each other. As this holds for every prime, $R$ is normal by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. This is the affine-local normality argument, with no assertion that the whole ring $R$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth, Zariski locality and affine ascent; Properties lemma-locally-normal, (1) implies (2), expanded using Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-normal-ring-normal] to the smooth ring map $\varphi:R\to S$ from step 2 and the normal ring $R$ from step 3. Its conclusion is that $S$ is normal: every $S_{\mathfrak q}$ for $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ is an integrally closed domain. The cited theorem assumes neither Noetherianity nor injectivity, faithful flatness, or connectedness.

source.place: Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth, affine ascent paragraph invoking Algebra Tag 033C, lemma-normal-goes-up.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q_v\subset S$ correspond to $v\in A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $S_{\mathfrak q_v}\simeq\mathcal O_{V,v}$. Step 4 and [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] make $S_{\mathfrak q_v}$ an integrally closed domain, and hence so is $\mathcal O_{V,v}$, by the ring-isomorphism argument in step 3. The point $v$ was arbitrary, giving precisely the asserted normality of $V$. If $V$ is empty the assertion is vacuous; if $W$ is empty the existence of $g$ forces $V$ to be empty. Nothing requires $g$ to be surjective, the charts to be connected, or either scheme to be quasi-compact or Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 034F, lemma-normal-local-smooth, Zariski locality and affine ascent; Properties definition-normal and lemma-locally-normal.
